Does Nesting Bias a Permutation Test?

Source: R/permutation_diagnostics.R
permutation_diagnostics.Rd

permutation_diagnostics() shows what treating nested sequences as independent costs a network comparison. It runs permutation() twice on the same networks and seed: once shuffling single sequences, once with actor, shuffling whole actors (the persons whose sessions the sequences are, or the teams of students). It returns the two results side by side, one row per compared pair or per edge, with the intraclass correlation (ICC) and design effect that explain any difference between them. It takes two transition networks, or every pair of groups of a netobject_group.

A design effect near 1 and few changed edges say that the nesting changes the comparison little. Where the two tests differ, the actor-level one is the test that follows the nesting, as permutation() sets out for nested data. The sections Nested data and actor and ICC and design effect of permutation() define these quantities, and How to read the result below says what each column shows.

Usage

permutation_diagnostics(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  actor,
  iter = 1000L,
  alpha = 0.05,
  level = c("overall", "edges"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

The networks to compare: a netobject_group, whose every pair of groups is diagnosed, or a netobject, compared with y. An mcml, whose layers hold different states, raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Only the transition methods "relative", "frequency" and "co_occurrence" are supported; any other method, association networks and wtna among them, raises an error of class nestimate_actor_unsupported.

y

The netobject to compare with when x is a netobject. Default NULL, as it must stay when x is a group.

actor

The column identifying the actor each sequence belongs to, as in permutation(), looked up in the networks' metadata or sequence data. A column not found, or one with missing values, raises an error of class nestimate_actor_missing. Required.

iter

The number of permutations for each of the two tests, at least 2. Default 1000.

alpha

The significance level that counts an edge as significant, between 0 and 1. The p-values are not adjusted for multiplicity. Default 0.05.

level

"overall" (default) returns one row per compared pair; "edges" one row per edge per pair.

seed

A seed for the shuffles, used by both tests, so the result repeats exactly. Default NULL.

Value

A data frame. With level = "overall", one row per compared pair:

pair

"<x> vs <y>", the names of the two groups ("x vs y" for two networks).

n_sequences, n_actors

The sequences and distinct actors in the pair.

design

"between" (every actor in one group), "within" (every actor in both groups) or "mixed".

icc, icc_ci_lower, icc_ci_upper

How alike the sequences of one actor are: the jackknife bias-corrected ICC, as printed by permutation(), with a 95% interval; with fewer than 3 actors the ICC is the uncorrected estimate and the interval is NA; the ICC is NA when no transition share varies.

deff_edges

The median over edges of the design effect, the ratio of the actor-level to the sequence-level null variance of the edge difference (Kish, 1965).

deff_global

The same ratio for the global M statistic.

p_global_sequence, p_global_actor

The permutation p-values of M when sequences or whole actors are reassigned.

sig_edges_sequence, sig_edges_actor

The number of edges with p < alpha under each test.

edges_changed

The number of edges significant under one test but not the other.

min_p_actor

The smallest p-value the actor-level test can reach: one over the number of distinct arrangements of the actors, or 1 / (iter + 1), whichever is larger.

With level = "edges", one row per edge present in either network, with the columns pair, from, to, diff (the observed difference, x - y), icc (the edge's ANOVA ICC, not bias-corrected; NA where the share does not vary), null_sd_sequence and null_sd_actor (the SD of the shuffled differences under each test), deff (NaN where the edge difference never varies under either null), p_sequence, p_actor and changed (whether the edge is significant under one test only).

The ICC and design effects are those of the actor-level run, as permutation() prints them when given actor; the p-values and significance counts compare it with a separate ordinary run.

How to read the result

deff_edges, deff_global

The design effect (Kish, 1965): actor-level over sequence-level null variance. 1 means the two shuffles give the same chance variation; above 1 the actor-level one varies more, below 1 less.

edges_changed

Edges significant under one test but not the other. Edges with p-values close to alpha can flip from Monte Carlo error alone; increase iter before reading much into one or two.

min_p_actor above alpha

Too few actors: the actor-level test cannot reject anything.

References

Efron, B., & Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). An Introduction to the Bootstrap. Chapman & Hall. (jackknife, ch. 11)

Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. Wiley. (design effect)

Anderson, M. J., & ter Braak, C. J. F. (2003). Permutation tests for multi-factorial analysis of variance. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 73(2), 85-113.

See also

permutation

Examples

# Students are nested in teams; Achiever is a team-level label.
# iter = 50 keeps the example fast; a real analysis uses 1000 or more.
net <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "relative",
                     actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time",
                     group = "Achiever")
permutation_diagnostics(net, actor = "Group", iter = 50, seed = 1)
#>          pair n_sequences n_actors  design          icc icc_ci_lower
#> 1 High vs Low        2000      200 between -0.001697397 -0.005641197
#>   icc_ci_upper deff_edges deff_global p_global_sequence p_global_actor
#> 1  0.002246402   1.069592    1.186787        0.01960784     0.01960784
#>   sig_edges_sequence sig_edges_actor edges_changed min_p_actor
#> 1                 38              42             4  0.01960784
head(permutation_diagnostics(net, actor = "Group", iter = 50,
                             level = "edges", seed = 1))
#>          pair  from         to         diff          icc null_sd_sequence
#> 1 High vs Low adapt   cohesion -0.014762566  0.010118088       0.03366031
#> 2 High vs Low adapt  consensus  0.055773975 -0.003796296       0.04581149
#> 3 High vs Low adapt coregulate -0.029891304  0.002498496       0.01144616
#> 4 High vs Low adapt    discuss -0.032473790 -0.009052931       0.02089267
#> 5 High vs Low adapt    emotion  0.030430928 -0.007376103       0.02759746
#> 6 High vs Low adapt    monitor -0.006957293 -0.003562251       0.01333857
#>   null_sd_actor      deff p_sequence    p_actor changed
#> 1    0.04169614 1.5344598 0.64705882 0.68627451   FALSE
#> 2    0.04532698 0.9789597 0.21568627 0.27450980   FALSE
#> 3    0.01121761 0.9604642 0.01960784 0.01960784   FALSE
